name: Comet Sighted
text: A searing streak of celestial fire has torn across the firmament, its luminous tail stretching from horizon to horizon like the blade of a cosmic executioner. The people gaze upward in a mixture of wonder and primal dread. Priests declare it a portent of divine wrath. Scholars reach for their instruments. Mothers clutch their children closer. The comet hangs above the nation like an unanswerable question, and its presence demands a response from the throne.

choices.text: Proclaim it a divine omen — let the people turn to prayer and sacrifice
The end is nigh — prepare the nation for the wrath to come
Study the heavens — there is knowledge written in those stars

name: Comet Spotted
text: Once more a comet blazes across the night sky, but this time the nation greets it not with terror but with the quiet confidence of an enlightened age. Telescopes track its parabolic arc across the heavens; newspapers print its orbital calculations; children sketch its shape in chalk upon the pavements. The primitive superstitions that once made our ancestors cower before such spectacles have been replaced by the steady light of reason. How far we have come.

choices.text: Thank the heavens we live in such enlightened times
Fund a new observatory to track future celestial phenomena

name: Artists Protest the Eiffel Tower
text: 'We, writers, painters, sculptors, architects, and passionate devotees of the hitherto untouched beauty of this nation, protest with all our strength and indignation, against the erection of this useless and monstrous Eiffel Tower. To bring our arguments home, imagine for a moment a giddy, ridiculous tower dominating this city like a gigantic black smokestack, crushing under its barbaric bulk Notre Dame, the Louvre, the Dome of the Invalides, the Arc de Triomphe, all of our humiliated monuments which will disappear in this ghastly dream.' The petition bears the signatures of forty-seven of the nation's most celebrated artists and intellectuals.

name: A Destitute Noble
text: A destitute nobleman has arrived at your court on a horse so gaunt its ribs protrude through its hide like the ribs of a shipwreck. He is without lord, without retinue, without coin — yet he carries himself with the unmistakable bearing of one born to command. His face is a palimpsest of scars, each one a testament to battles fought and survived. His armor, though tarnished and dented, bears the crest of a house that once ruled vast territories. He kneels before your throne and pledges his sword, his name, and his remaining years to your service.

choices.text: Turn him away — we have no need of fallen men and their fallen fortunes
Outfit him with fresh armor and a command in the vanguard
Seize what remains of his estate, then execute him — no rival house may rise from the ashes
Welcome him as a court advisor — his experience is worth more than his sword arm

name: The Guest Star
text: The year is 1054. A new star has erupted in the heavens, blazing forth in the constellation Taurus with a brilliance that rivals Venus herself. It is visible even at midday — a searing point of white fire suspended against the blue. Court astronomers call it a 'guest star,' a celestial visitor of unknown provenance. It will remain visible for nearly two years, during which time it will slowly fade, leaving behind a slowly expanding nebula of gas and dust. But for now, it burns, and the entire nation stares skyward in astonishment.

choices.text: Such terrible beauty — commission artists to capture this divine spectacle
An astronomical miracle — record every detail for the scholars of generations to come
A sign from the heavens — build a temple to honor this celestial messenger

name: Solar Eclipse
text: The nation stares upward in collective terror as the Sun — that eternal, dependable orb of warmth and light — is slowly devoured by an unseen black disc. The sky deepens to an unnatural twilight. Birds fall silent. Temperatures drop. Shadows take on an eerie, crescent-shaped quality. The people clutch one another, weep, pray, and sacrifice. Then, after an eternity measured in minutes, the Sun returns, sliver by sliver, until it blazes forth once more in full glory. The nation exhales.

choices.text: Our prayers and sacrifices have brought back the light — redouble our devotion
There must be a rational explanation — summon the scholars to investigate
The gods are angry with our enemies — this omen foretells their destruction

name: Struck Oil!
text: Glorious news from the oil fields! Workers expanding an existing well have struck a massive subterranean reservoir of crude oil so pressurized that the black gold erupted from the earth in a geyser that could be seen for miles. The smell of hydrocarbons hangs over the region like the scent of future prosperity. Geologists estimate this new vein could double our output for weeks, perhaps months. The industrial implications are staggering.

choices.text: Wonderful news — pump it dry and fuel the nation's engines
Sell the surplus on the international market — let the profits flow

name: A Beast Stalks the City
text: Rumors have begun to slink through the capital like fog through alleyways. Something stalks the city streets in the deepest hours of the night — something large, something feral, something that should not exist within the walls of a civilized settlement. Eyewitness accounts vary wildly and contradict one another at every turn: some swear it is a demon with eyes of ember and a stench of sulfur; others describe a monstrous wolf of unnatural size; one particularly imaginative drunk insists it is a 'wild haggis' — whatever that may be. Livestock has gone missing. A child's shoe was found near the river, its owner nowhere to be seen. The city grows restless.

choices.text: I do not address mere rumors — let the constables handle the rabble
Dispatch a squad of guards to track and slay the creature
Capture it alive — put it on display in a menagerie and charge admission
I shall hunt this beast myself — saddle my horse and ready my spear

name: Miracle Harvest!
text: Reports pour in from every province, every village, every farmstead — and the story is the same everywhere. The earth has yielded with an almost supernatural generosity this season. Granaries overflow. Flour mills grind ceaselessly. Bakeries cannot keep pace with demand. Children who have known only meager portions now sit before plates heaped with bread, fruit, and roasted grain. The discovery of new fertilization techniques, combined with an almost perfect sequence of rainfall and sunshine, has produced what old farmers are calling 'the harvest of a lifetime.' Some are calling it a miracle.

choices.text: Food for all — let no citizen go hungry this winter
Store the surplus against future famine — wisdom demands preparation
Export the excess to neighboring nations — profit from nature's generosity

name: Social Reforms
text: Your advisors have spent months drafting a sweeping package of social reforms — labor protections, expanded education, restructured taxation, and a reimagining of the social contract between governed and government. The proposals are bold, visionary, and deeply controversial. The merchant guilds are already mobilizing opposition. The priesthood is divided. The military watches with cautious eyes. But the common people — the laborers, the farmers, the artisans — they whisper of these reforms with a desperate, hungry hope. The decision falls to you.

choices.text: No — such drastic changes will tear this nation apart, not mend it
Implement the reforms in full — the people deserve a better future
Those who proposed such dangerous ideas are traitors — execute them as a warning
Implement the reforms gradually — a measured approach will appease all sides

name: Nationalize the Utilities
text: A fierce debate has gripped the halls of power. The nation's essential industries — water, power, transport, communications — are currently in private hands, owned by a constellation of wealthy industrialists and foreign conglomerates. Your economic advisors argue that nationalizing these sectors would ensure equitable access for all citizens and redirect profits toward public works. The industrialists, predictably, are apoplectic with rage and have threatened capital flight, legal action, and political retaliation. The decision carries consequences either way.

choices.text: These industries shall remain private — the free market knows best
For the People — nationalize these essential services at once
Negotiate a partial nationalization — key sectors only, with compensation

name: Subsidize
text: Traffic in the capital has reached a crisis point. Carts, carriages, and pedestrians choke the thoroughfares from dawn to dusk, and the resulting paralysis costs the nation dearly in lost productivity, missed shipments, and frayed tempers. Your urban planners have drawn up two competing proposals for a mass transit system that could untangle the gridlock and restore the free flow of people and goods through the city's arteries. Each plan carries a different vision of the future.

choices.text: Expand bus and tram routes — a flexible, above-ground network serving all districts
Fund an underground subway — a grand engineering project for the ages

name: Mystic
text: An itinerant mystic has appeared at the gates of the capital, barefoot and robed in undyed linen, carrying nothing but a wooden bowl and a staff carved with symbols no scholar can decipher. He has planted fruit trees in the commons and brewed spiced cider from their first yield. Crowds gather around him by the hundreds, then the thousands — sharing food, listening to his parables, weeping at his words. He speaks of love, of simplicity, of the divine spark within every soul. Some call him a prophet. Others call him a madman. The authorities are uncertain which designation is more dangerous.

choices.text: Listen to his sermons — there may be wisdom hidden in his simplicity
Take up his cider and share it with the nation — let his generosity spread
Silence him — I deal with enough madmen without inviting more to my doorstep

name: Harvest
text: The harvest has exceeded all expectations this year. Granaries groan under the weight of sheaves. Flour mills grind day and night, their wheels never still. Bakeries send the scent of fresh bread wafting through every street and lane. Farmers who have known lean years now count their blessings with trembling hands. The earth has been generous, and the nation shall eat well this winter.

choices.text: A glorious harvest for a glorious year — let the people feast
Hold a harvest festival — celebrate the bounty with music and dance

name: Famine
text: The harvest has failed. Not merely in one region, but across the nation. The spring rains never came. The summer heat withered the crops in their fields. Autumn brought locusts in clouds so thick they darkened the sky. Now winter approaches, and the granaries stand nearly empty. Flour mills have gone silent. Bakeries display bare shelves. The poor queue in lines that stretch for blocks, holding bowls that will be filled with thin gruel, if they are filled at all. Children cry with a hunger that no parent can satisfy. The nation looks to its ruler for salvation.

choices.text: Who could have cursed this land with famine — we must find the culprit
Open the royal granaries — no citizen shall starve while we have reserves
Ration what remains — the strong will survive, the weak will not

name: Desertion
text: The war has ground on far longer than anyone anticipated. Letters from the front describe mud, disease, and death in equal measure. Morale has collapsed. Soldiers are slipping away from their posts under cover of darkness, filtering back toward their homes through back roads and forests. Entire companies have reported losses not to enemy action but to desertion. Your generals warn that if the hemorrhage continues, the army will simply dissolve. The troops who remain are watching closely to see how you respond.

choices.text: There is nothing to be done — tell the generals to bear this burden as best they can

Court-martial the deserters — let the law take its course with due process

But the question of how to harness this intellectual surge remains open. Pure research? Military application? Public education? Each path leads somewhere different, and the resources to pursue all of them do not exist.

The magnificent artworks that once lined every corridor now lie buried beneath layers of dust and grime so thick that their frames are barely distinguishable from the walls. Rain leaks through the roof in places where roof should not leak. The building is a monument to neglect, and it is no longer fit to house the government of a great nation.

name: The Black Death
text: Death has arrived at your shores, carried on the backs of rats scurrying through the holds of merchant vessels. The sickness begins with a fever, then swollen lymph nodes the size of eggs, then purple-black splotches beneath the skin, then death — often within three days, sometimes within a single night. The plague spreads with a speed that defies containment. Bodies pile in the streets. Priests refuse to administer last rites. Entire villages vanish from the map in a matter of weeks. The nation has not faced a catastrophe of this magnitude since the fall of antiquity.

choices.text: Quarantine the afflicted cities — seal the gates and let no one enter or leave

name: Great Earthquake
text: Without warning, the earth beneath your nation convulses with a violence that beggars description. The ground heaves like the deck of a ship in a hurricane. Buildings sway, crack, and collapse in cascading avalanches of stone and timber. The air fills with dust, screams, and the grinding roar of shifting tectonic plates. When the shaking finally subsides, the landscape is unrecognizable — roads split open, bridges fallen, entire districts reduced to rubble. The survivors stumble through the wreckage, calling out the names of those who will never answer.

choices.text: Rebuild immediately — marshal every resource we have to restore the nation
Let the people rebuild on their own — the treasury cannot absorb this loss
Rebuild smarter — impose new construction codes to resist future quakes

name: Volcanic Eruption
text: The mountain that has loomed peacefully over the eastern provinces for as long as anyone can remember has revealed its true nature. First came the tremors, growing in intensity over several days. Then the summit cracked open like an egg, belching a column of fire and ash miles into the stratosphere. Rivers of molten rock now cascade down the flanks, consuming everything in their path. Ash rains from the sky in thick, suffocating curtains, turning day to night. The destruction is vast, but the fertile ash may one day yield extraordinary harvests.

choices.text: Evacuate the eastern provinces — save what lives we can
Hold fast and wait for the eruption to subside — the ash will enrich the soil
Study the eruption — such geological events are rare and hold scientific value

name: The Silk Road Opens
text: Reports arrive from your frontier scouts of a vast network of trade routes stretching eastward through deserts, over mountain passes, and across steppes to civilizations of unimaginable wealth and sophistication. Silk that feels like liquid light. Spices that transform the humblest meal into a feast. Jade, porcelain, and incense of qualities never before seen in your markets. The merchants of your nation are practically vibrating with excitement. The potential for profit — and cultural exchange — is staggering.

choices.text: Fund a major trade expedition — spare no expense in establishing these routes
Send diplomats alongside the merchants — build alliances as we build wealth

name: Religious Schism
text: A theological dispute that began as a quarrel among scholars has erupted into a full-blown schism that threatens to tear the faithful apart. Two competing interpretations of the sacred texts have gained massive followings, and the disagreement has moved beyond the realm of intellectual debate. Tempers flare in the streets. Rival congregations eye one another with suspicion across market squares. The clergy itself is divided, with prominent leaders declaring for opposing doctrines. The unity of the faith hangs by a thread, and the thread is fraying.

choices.text: Support the reformers — the faith must evolve or perish
Defend the orthodox doctrine — tradition must be preserved at all costs
Mediate a compromise — find common ground and heal the rift

name: The Printing Press
text: A craftsman in your capital has achieved something that will reshape the very fabric of civilization. Using movable type and a converted wine press, he has produced pages of text at a speed and consistency that makes the labors of scribes look like the scratching of children. Books — once the exclusive province of monasteries and kings — can now be produced by the hundreds, the thousands. Knowledge, that most precious and most hoarded of commodities, is about to flood the nation like water through a broken dam. The implications are staggering, and not all of them are beneficial.

choices.text: Subsidize the printing of books — let knowledge flow to every corner of the nation
Control the presses — only approved texts may be printed
Let the market decide — whoever can afford a press may print whatever they wish

name: Royal Wedding
text: An opportunity has presented itself to forge a dynastic alliance through marriage. A foreign royal house of considerable power and influence has offered the hand of their heir to a member of your own family. The match is politically advantageous, culturally significant, and personally complicated — the prospective bride or groom has a reputation that precedes them across several kingdoms. Nevertheless, the diplomatic benefits of such a union are substantial and potentially game-changing.

A barbarian horde — the largest assembled in living memory — is marching toward your borders. Thousands of warriors on horseback, their ranks swelled by disaffected tribes and desperate refugees from every direction. They are not merely raiding. They are coming to conquer. The nation must respond, and quickly.

name: Gold Rush

He claims to have discovered a massive deposit in the hills to the north — veins of gold visible to the naked eye, glittering in the stream beds like the floor of a river in paradise. Within days, the roads are clogged with fortune-seekers, dreamers, and desperadoes of every description. The nation holds its breath as a stampede of humanity surges toward the gold fields.

name: The Great Library Burns
text: Flames have engulfed the Great Library. The fire began in the eastern wing and spread with a ferocity that overwhelmed the efforts of every bucket brigade in the city. Centuries of accumulated knowledge — scrolls documenting the wisdom of philosophers, the discoveries of scientists, the histories of empires, the poetry of ages — are being reduced to ash and cinder. Scholars stand in the streets, weeping openly as the smoke of a thousand lifetimes of learning rises into the night sky. Some works can be saved. Most cannot. The question is what to save.

choices.text: Save the scientific and technical texts — knowledge of the natural world is most valuable
Save the literary and historical works — the soul of the nation lies in its stories
Save everything you can carry — grab whatever is nearest and run
Rush into the flames yourself — no sacrifice is too great for the preservation of knowledge

name: Market Crash
text: The floor of the national stock exchange has become a theater of financial apocalypse. Prices that climbed for years on a ladder of speculation and borrowed money are now falling with a velocity that defies comprehension. Brokers stare at ticker tapes in disbelief, then crumple the paper in their fists. Fortunes built over decades evaporate in minutes. Banks close their doors. Businesses shutter their windows. The ripple effects are already spreading outward from the financial district into every corner of the economy, and from there into every home in the nation.

choices.text: Inject government funds to stabilize the markets — the nation cannot afford a collapse
Let the market correct itself — government intervention will only prolong the pain
Seize the opportunity — buy up failed businesses and assets at fire-sale prices

name: Medical Breakthrough
text: Your nation's physicians have achieved something miraculous. After years of painstaking research, trial and error, and more than a few tragic failures, they have developed a treatment that could save countless lives. The disease that has been the leading cause of death in your nation — the one that carries off children, mothers, and soldiers alike — may finally be conquerable. The implications for public health, military readiness, and economic productivity are immense. The question is how to deploy this gift.

choices.text: Distribute the treatment freely to all citizens — health is a right, not a privilege
Patent the treatment and sell it internationally — let it fund further research
Reserve it for the military and the elite — the masses will breed regardless

name: The Olympic Games
text: Athletes from across the known world have gathered in a spirit of peaceful competition and physical excellence. The games are a spectacle unlike any other — a celebration of the human body pushed to its absolute limits, of nations setting aside their quarrels to compete in arenas of sport rather than fields of battle. Your nation has been invited to participate, and the decision carries implications far beyond athletics. Glory on the field can translate to prestige on the world stage.

choices.text: Sponsor our finest athletes — spare no expense in pursuit of glory
Send a modest delegation — participate with dignity but without extravagance
Decline to participate — such frivolities are beneath a serious nation

name: World's Fair
text: An international exposition of unprecedented scale and ambition is being organized, and your nation has been invited to participate. Nations from across the globe will converge to display their greatest achievements in industry, science, art, and culture. It is at once a trade show, a diplomatic summit, and a contest of national prestige. The host city will become, for a season, the capital of the world. The opportunity to showcase your civilization's finest accomplishments is extraordinary — but so is the cost of doing so properly.

choices.text: Host the exposition — let the world marvel at our greatness
Participate with a grand pavilion — showcase our achievements without hosting
Send a modest exhibit — participate without overcommitting our resources

name: Immigration Wave
text: Tens of thousands of people are streaming across your borders, fleeing war, famine, and persecution in their homelands. They arrive with little but the clothes on their backs and a desperate determination to build new lives. Among them are farmers, artisans, scholars, soldiers, and families with children who have known nothing but displacement. Your border officials are overwhelmed. The nation's capacity to absorb this influx is being tested to its limits, and the question of whether to welcome or turn away these refugees has ignited passionate debate across every stratum of society.

choices.text: Open the borders — these people bring skills, labor, and diversity that will enrich us
Accept only the skilled and educated — we need talent, not mouths to feed
Seal the borders — our people come first, always and without exception

name: Labor Strike
text: The factories have gone silent. Not from mechanical failure or lack of materials, but from the collective refusal of the workforce to continue laboring under conditions they describe as intolerable. Tens of thousands of workers have walked off the job, picketing the factory gates with signs demanding shorter hours, safer conditions, and wages that can actually feed a family. The industrialists demand that you send in the army to break the strike. The workers demand that you hear their grievances. The economy bleeds with every hour that passes without resolution.

choices.text: Side with the workers — mandate better conditions and fairer wages
Side with the industrialists — send in the army to restore order
Mediate a compromise — bring both sides to the table and negotiate

name: Espionage Uncovered
text: Your intelligence service has captured a foreign spy in the heart of the capital, in possession of documents of the most sensitive nature — military deployments, diplomatic communications, economic assessments. The spy has been subjected to interrogation and has revealed the identity of a network of informants operating within your own government. The breach is severe, the betrayal deep, and the political fallout threatens to engulf both domestic and foreign relations in chaos.

choices.text: Execute the spy publicly — send a message that espionage against us carries a fatal price
Quietly return the spy to their homeland in exchange for concessions
Turn the spy into a double agent — feed disinformation back to their masters

name: Natural Wonder Discovery
text: Your explorers have pushed beyond the known edges of the map and returned with tales that strain the bounds of credulity. They describe a landscape of such breathtaking, otherworldly beauty that their words falter and their eyes grow distant with the memory of it. Geysers erupting in rhythmic columns of steam. Waterfalls cascading from cliffs taller than any cathedral. Valleys carpeted in flowers of colors that have no name in your language. Canyons carved so deep by rivers of time that their walls glow in bands of red, gold, and violet. The discovery will echo through the ages.

choices.text: Preserve the wonder as a national treasure — protect it for all eternity
Develop it as a tourist destination — let the world pay to witness its splendor
Study the geological formations — science may learn from this natural laboratory

name: Mining Disaster
text: A catastrophic collapse has entombed hundreds of miners deep beneath the earth. The initial reports are fragmentary and desperate — a tunnel gave way without warning, burying men, women, and children (for in some mines, children still work the seams) beneath tons of rock and earth. Rescue teams have been assembled, but the situation underground is dire. The shafts are unstable. The air is thin. Time is running out for those trapped below. Above ground, families gather at the mine entrance, their faces a portrait of anguish and desperate hope.

choices.text: Spare no expense on the rescue effort — every life is worth any cost
Mount a rescue within reasonable limits — we cannot bankrupt the nation for one mine
Seal the mine and move on — the risk to rescuers is too great

name: Slave Revolt
text: The chains have been broken. Across the plantations and estates, the enslaved have risen with a fury forged in generations of bondage. Armed with farm tools, stolen weapons, and a rage that burns hotter than any furnace, they have overwhelmed their overseers and seized control of entire districts. The roads are choked with refugees fleeing the violence. The mansions of the wealthy are in flames. The revolt spreads with each passing hour, and the question of how to respond grows more urgent with every report of fresh atrocities on both sides.

choices.text: Crush the revolt with overwhelming military force — restore order at any cost

choices.text: Abolish slavery and offer the rebels full citizenship — end the injustice that caused this
Negotiate a gradual emancipation — free the slaves over time while compensating owners

name: Constitutional Convention
text: The old order has buckled under the weight of its own contradictions, and the nation stands at a crossroads. Delegates from every province, every faction, every interest group have assembled in the capital to draft a new framework for governance — a constitution that will define the relationship between the state and the citizen for generations to come. The debates are fierce, the disagreements fundamental, and the stakes nothing less than the soul of the nation. The question of how much power to vest in the central authority versus the liberties of the individual has fractured the convention into warring camps.

choices.text: Draft a constitution that centralizes authority — order and stability above all
Draft a constitution that enshrines individual liberties — freedom above all
Draft a balanced constitution — compromise between authority and liberty

name: The Enlightenment
text: A great awakening of the intellect is sweeping through the salons, universities, and coffee houses of the nation. Philosophers are publishing treatises that challenge the very foundations of authority — divine right, inherited privilege, the unquestioned wisdom of tradition. They speak of natural rights, of the social contract, of the sovereignty of reason over superstition. The old guard is horrified. The young are electrified. The printers cannot keep up with demand. The nation's intellectual life has caught fire, and the flames show no sign of abating.

choices.text: Embrace the new philosophy — fund the thinkers and reform the institutions
Tolerate the philosophers but offer no official support — let ideas compete freely
Suppress these dangerous ideas — they threaten the very fabric of civilization

name: Pirate Attack
text: Word reaches the capital that a flotilla of pirate vessels has been terrorizing your coastal trade routes. Merchant ships have been boarded, their cargoes seized, their crews set adrift in dinghies with nothing but a compass and a taunting farewell. The pirates are bold, well-armed, and operating from a hidden base somewhere along a stretch of coastline too rugged and too remote for your naval forces to easily reach. The economic losses are mounting, and the merchants are demanding action.

choices.text: Dispatch the navy to hunt them down — scour every cove and inlet
Hire privateers to deal with the pirates — fight fire with fire
Pay them off and negotiate safe passage — it is cheaper than fighting

name: University Founding
text: A consortium of scholars, wealthy patrons, and civic leaders has proposed the establishment of a great university — an institution dedicated to the pursuit of knowledge across every discipline known to humanity. The plans are ambitious: lecture halls, laboratories, libraries, dormitories, botanical gardens, and an observatory. If built, it would become the intellectual heart of the nation, attracting the finest minds from across the known world. The cost is considerable, but the potential returns are incalculable.

choices.text: Fund the university in full — make it the greatest center of learning in the world
Provide partial funding — let private patrons cover the rest
Grant a charter but no funds — let the scholars raise the money themselves

name: Nuclear Meltdown
text: An alarm has sounded at the nation's primary nuclear power facility. A cascade of failures — coolant loss, reactor overheating, containment breach — has triggered a situation that the engineers are struggling to bring under control. Radiation is leaking into the surrounding area. Evacuation orders have gone out to every settlement within fifty kilometers. The plant's workforce is performing acts of extraordinary bravery in an attempt to prevent a total catastrophe, but the outcome remains uncertain. The political and environmental consequences of this event will reverberate for decades.

choices.text: Order a full evacuation and sacrifice the plant — save the people, write off the investment
Send in emergency teams to contain the meltdown — minimize the damage at any cost
Suppress all information and deny that anything happened

name: Space Race Milestone
text: Your nation's space program has achieved a historic first — a milestone that will be remembered as long as humanity endures. The achievement has captivated not only your own citizens but the entire world. Children who were indifferent about their studies now dream of becoming astronauts. Scientists who toiled in obscurity are suddenly household names. The nation stands taller on the world stage, and the implications for science, prestige, and national pride are immense. The question is how to capitalize on this moment of glory.

choices.text: Double the space program's budget — push onward to even greater achievements
Leverage the achievement for international prestige and diplomatic leverage
Redirect the space program's budget toward domestic priorities

name: Environmental Awakening
text: A movement has taken root in the nation, born of a growing recognition that the relentless pursuit of industrial progress has come at a terrible cost. Rivers that once teemed with fish now run thick with chemical runoff. Forests that stood for millennia have been reduced to stumps and mud. The very air in the cities has become a brown haze that stings the eyes and rasps the lungs. Scientists are beginning to speak of long-term consequences that could be irreversible. The people are demanding action, and the industrialists are demanding to be left alone.

choices.text: Implement strict environmental regulations — the planet must come before profit
Balance regulation with economic reality — gradual reforms, not revolution
Reject the environmentalists — economic growth is the only path to prosperity

name: Cultural Flowering
text: Something extraordinary is happening in the studios, theaters, and concert halls of the nation. A wave of creative energy unlike anything in living memory has swept through the artistic community. Painters are producing canvases that make viewers weep. Composers are writing symphonies that bring audiences to their feet. Playwrights are crafting works that provoke, challenge, and transform. Writers are producing novels that will be read for centuries. The nation's cultural life has erupted into a blaze of brilliance that shows no sign of dimming.

choices.text: Patronize the arts lavishly — make our nation the cultural capital of the world
Let the artistic community flourish naturally — genius cannot be bought, only nurtured
Channel the creative energy into propaganda — art in service of the state

name: Drought
text: The rains have not come. Month after month, the skies remain a pitiless, cloudless blue. Crops wither in the fields, their stalks curling inward like the fingers of a dying man. Rivers shrink to trickles, then to nothing. Wells that have never run dry in living memory now echo hollowly when a stone is dropped into their depths. Livestock collapse in the pastures, their tongues black and swollen. The land is dying of thirst, and the people are not far behind.

choices.text: Organize massive relief efforts — import food and water at any cost
Ration what water remains — strict allocation for all citizens
Invest in irrigation infrastructure — solve the problem for the future, not just today

name: Great Flood
text: The river has broken its banks. Not gradually, not with the slow inevitability of a rising tide, but with a sudden, roaring violence that swept away everything in its path. Entire villages have been submerged. Farmlands that fed thousands now lie beneath meters of muddy water. The flood came so fast that many had no time to flee — they clung to rooftops, to treetops, to anything that floated, and watched their world disappear beneath the brown, debris-choked torrent. The waters are receding now, but what they have left behind is a landscape of devastation.

choices.text: Launch a massive reconstruction effort — rebuild everything better than before
Provide basic relief and let the people rebuild on their own
Construct flood defenses to ensure this never happens again

name: The Renaissance Man
text: A figure of almost supernatural versatility has emerged from the workshops and academies of your nation. He is an artist who paints with the precision of a surgeon, an engineer who designs fortifications that military experts call revolutionary, an anatomist whose dissections have overturned centuries of medical dogma, a musician, a poet, an inventor, and a visionary who seems to glimpse the future with a clarity that borders on the prophetic. His notebooks are filled with designs for flying machines, diving apparatuses, and mechanical knights. The world has not seen his like since antiquity, and may not see it again.

choices.text: Shower him with patronage — give him every resource to pursue his visions
Direct his genius toward military engineering — we need weapons, not paintings

choices.text: Let him work independently — genius cannot be directed, only admired

name: Industrial Revolution
text: The workshops of the nation are transforming before your eyes. Hand looms are giving way to mechanized spinning jennies. Water wheels are being supplemented — and in some cases replaced — by hissing, pounding steam engines that turn coal into motion with an efficiency that borders on the magical. The smoke of a thousand new factories darkens the sky. The clatter of machinery drowns out the sounds of birdsong. Production is soaring. Wealth is accumulating. And the social fabric is straining under the weight of changes so profound that no one can predict where they will lead.

choices.text: Embrace the revolution fully — subsidize industry and accelerate the transformation
Guide the revolution with regulation — protect workers while encouraging growth
Resist the revolution — protect traditional crafts and ways of life

name: Women's Suffrage Movement
text: A movement that has been building for decades has finally reached the steps of the legislature. Women from every class, every region, and every walk of life have organized, petitioned, protested, and persisted in the face of ridicule, dismissal, and outright hostility. They demand the right to vote, to hold office, to participate fully in the governance of the nation they help build and defend. The traditionalists are appalled. The progressives are energized. The political establishment is caught between the irresistible force of change and the immovable object of custom.

choices.text: Grant full suffrage — it is long overdue and morally right
Grant suffrage gradually — start with local elections and expand over time
Reject the demand — the traditional order exists for a reason

name: The Great Depression
text: The economic collapse that began in the financial sector has spread to every corner of the economy like a plague transmitted through the bloodstream of commerce itself. Factories stand idle. Shops are shuttered. Bread lines stretch for blocks. Unemployed men sell apples on street corners for a penny apiece. Families who were comfortable a year ago now face eviction and starvation. The nation's confidence has been shattered, and with it, the consumption that drives the engine of prosperity. The government must act, but how — and how boldly — remains the question that will define this generation.

choices.text: Launch massive public works programs — put the nation back to work building its future
Cut taxes and reduce government spending — let the free market heal itself
Provide direct relief to the poorest — keep the nation alive while the economy recovers

name: Meteor Shower
text: The night sky has erupted into a celestial fireworks display of breathtaking magnificence. Thousands of meteors are streaking across the heavens in a dazzling cascade of light, leaving luminous trails that linger for seconds before fading into the darkness. The spectacle is visible across the entire nation, and people have poured out of their homes to gaze upward in collective wonder. Children point and shout. Lovers hold hands and make wishes. Astronomers scramble for their instruments. It is a reminder, beautiful and humbling, that the Earth is but a small vessel adrift in a vast and active cosmos.

choices.text: Declare it a national celebration — such beauty must be honored
Dispatch astronomers to study the phenomenon — there is science in those lights
Interpret it as a divine sign — redouble the nation's spiritual devotion

name: Trade Wind Discovery
text: Your navigators have mapped a pattern of ocean currents and prevailing winds that could revolutionize maritime trade. By following these currents, ships can reach distant markets in a fraction of the time previously required, and with far less risk of being becalmed or blown off course. The implications for commerce, exploration, and naval strategy are immense. The knowledge is valuable, but the question of how to exploit it — and whether to share it — carries significant strategic weight.

choices.text: Keep the routes secret — let our merchants enjoy a monopoly on faster trade
Share the knowledge freely — let all nations benefit from faster commerce
Use the routes for naval supremacy — project power across the oceans

name: Cuban Missile Crisis
text: The world holds its breath. Satellite imagery has confirmed what intelligence agencies feared: a hostile superpower is installing nuclear missiles within striking distance of your major cities. The weapons, once operational, could reduce your civilization to radioactive ash within thirty minutes of launch. Your military advisors are presenting options ranging from a preemptive strike to a naval blockade to diplomatic negotiation. Every option carries the risk of triggering a full-scale nuclear exchange — a war that no one would win, and from which no one would recover. The clock is ticking.

choices.text: Impose a naval blockade — show strength without crossing the point of no return
Negotiate directly with the opposing leader — find a diplomatic resolution
Launch a preemptive strike — destroy the missiles before they can be armed

name: The Internet Age
text: A new technology has emerged that promises to reshape the very architecture of human civilization. A global network of interconnected computers — an 'internet' — allows the instantaneous exchange of information across continents, oceans, and political boundaries. Knowledge that once required a journey to a great library can now be accessed from a device that fits in the palm of a hand. Commerce, culture, politics, and personal relationships are all being radically transformed. The implications are exhilarating and terrifying in equal measure.

choices.text: Invest heavily in digital infrastructure — make our nation the most connected on Earth
Regulate the network carefully — protect citizens from its dangers while harnessing its benefits
Monitor and control the flow of information — this technology is too powerful to leave unregulated

name: The Pandemic
text: A novel pathogen has emerged from an unexpected corner of the world and begun spreading with a speed that has overwhelmed every public health system it has encountered. The disease is stealthy — carriers can transmit it for days before showing symptoms — and deadly, with a mortality rate that has hospitals operating beyond capacity and morgues running out of space. Borders are closing. Supply chains are fracturing. The global economy is shuddering. Your nation's first cases have just been confirmed, and the window for decisive action is closing rapidly.

choices.text: Implement a full national lockdown — save lives now, count the economic cost later
Targeted restrictions only — protect the vulnerable while keeping the economy running
Keep the nation open and let the disease run its course — the economy cannot stop
Mobilize the entire scientific establishment to find a cure or vaccine

name: The Silk Road Closes
text: The great trade routes that have carried silk, spice, and precious metals between east and west for centuries are being severed. A vast empire to the east has closed its borders to foreign merchants. The caravans have stopped. The markets that thrived on the exchange of goods and ideas are falling silent. The economic impact is immediate and severe, but the cultural consequences — the slow strangulation of the cross-pollination of civilizations — may prove even more devastating in the long run.

choices.text: Find alternative sea routes — if the land is closed, the ocean remains open
Develop domestic industries to replace lost imports — self-sufficiency is the answer
Negotiate aggressively with the eastern empire — remind them of what they stand to lose

name: Cultural Revolution
text: A charismatic leader has galvanized the youth of the nation into a movement that promises to sweep away the old order and build a new society from the rubble. The movement's ideology is radical, its methods are uncompromising, and its followers are fanatically devoted. Universities have been shut down. Professors have been publicly humiliated. Ancient monuments are being torn from their pedestals. The old guard watches in horror as everything they built is dismantled before their eyes. The question is whether to ride this wave or resist it.

choices.text: Embrace the revolution — let the old order burn and a new one rise from the ashes
Co-opt the movement — channel its energy toward productive national goals
Suppress the movement with force — restore order and preserve the nation's heritage

name: The Great Migration
text: Your scouts and border officials report an unprecedented movement of peoples across the landscape. Not an army, not a refugee column, but an entire nation on the march — families, herds, carts, and warriors stretching from horizon to horizon. They are not hostile, at least not yet. They are seeking new lands to settle, driven from their ancestral homes by drought, war, or famine. Their numbers are vast enough to reshape the demographics of any region they enter. The decision of how to respond will define your nation's character for generations.

choices.text: Welcome them as citizens — their labor and diversity will strengthen the nation
Offer them land in the frontier regions — let them buffer the nation against external threats
Turn them away — our land is for our people, and our resources are not infinite

name: Assassination
text: An assassin's blade has struck down a figure of enormous consequence — a beloved leader, a controversial monarch, or a pivotal reformer whose policies were reshaping the nation. The killer has been apprehended, but the motives remain murky, and the conspiracy may extend far beyond a single hand. The nation is in shock. Grief and rage compete for dominance in the streets. Some demand vengeance. Others demand answers. The political vacuum left by this act will be filled by something — the only question is what.

choices.text: Launch a sweeping investigation and purge every trace of the conspiracy
Channel the national grief into unity — honor the fallen and continue their work
Use the assassination as a pretext to consolidate power — never let a crisis go to waste

name: The Reformation Begins
text: A monk has nailed a document to the door of a church, and the sound of those hammer-blows is echoing across the continent. His theses — ninety-five points of theological dispute — have been reproduced by the printing press and distributed faster than any authority can suppress them. He challenges the corruption of the clergy, the sale of divine forgiveness for gold, and the very structure of religious authority. The establishment is outraged. The common people are electrified. A schism is opening that will not be healed, and the political order built upon the old faith will not survive it intact.

choices.text: Embrace the reformer's ideas — purge the corruption and renew the faith
Condemn the reformer — defend the traditional church and its authority
Remain neutral — let the theologians fight their battles while we govern

name: Tornado Outbreak
text: A swarm of tornadoes has torn across the heartland of the nation with a savagery that defies comprehension. The funnels — some a mile wide, their winds exceeding anything ever measured — have scoured the earth bare, reducing entire towns to matchsticks and rubble. The destruction follows a path hundreds of miles long, a scar of devastation visible from the air. Survivors emerge from root cellars and storm shelters to find their homes, their barns, their churches, and their schools simply gone. The rebuilding will take years. The trauma will take generations.

choices.text: Mobilize the full resources of the state for reconstruction
Provide emergency relief and let local communities rebuild
Invest in early warning systems to prevent future catastrophes

name: The Great Awakening
text: A religious revival of extraordinary intensity has swept through the nation like a wildfire through dry brush. Preachers with voices like thunder and eyes like burning coals have drawn crowds of tens of thousands to open-air gatherings that last for days. Weeping, singing, confessing, and converting, the people have been seized by a spiritual fervor that transcends denomination and defies institutional control. The established churches are uncertain whether to embrace this movement or fear it. The political authorities are equally divided.

choices.text: Embrace the revival — let the nation's spirit be renewed
Channel the fervor into social reform — faith without works is dead
Keep the revival at arm's length — religious ecstasy and political stability are poor companions

name: The Canal Project
text: Your engineers have proposed a project of staggering ambition: the construction of a canal that will cut through the narrow isthmus connecting two continents, uniting two oceans and slashing weeks from the journey between them. The economic implications are enormous — trade routes will be redrawn, fortunes will be made, and the nation that controls the canal will hold a chokepoint of global commerce. The engineering challenges are formidable, the cost is astronomical, and the human toll will be measured in the thousands. But the prize is nothing less than geopolitical dominance.

choices.text: Fund the project in full — build the canal and claim its strategic value
Seek international partners to share the cost and the benefits
Reject the project — the risks and costs outweigh the potential benefits

name: The Scientific Revolution
text: A paradigm shift of seismic proportions is rocking the foundations of human knowledge. The old certainties — the Earth at the center of the universe, the body governed by four humors, the heavens operating on immutable principles — are crumbling before a new method of inquiry that demands evidence, experimentation, and mathematical proof. Astronomers are mapping orbits that defy ancient doctrine. Physicists are formulating laws that govern motion and force with unprecedented precision. The universe is revealing itself to be far stranger, far vaster, and far more mechanical than anyone imagined.

choices.text: Establish a national academy of sciences — make our nation the vanguard of the new knowledge
Support the scientists but let them work independently — genius cannot be commanded
Resist these dangerous ideas — they undermine faith, tradition, and social order

name: The Abolition of Slavery
text: A moral reckoning has arrived at the doors of the nation. The practice of human bondage — embedded in the economy, enshrined in law, and justified by centuries of tradition — is under assault as never before. Abolitionists have mounted a campaign of such moral force and rhetorical power that the institution of slavery is being questioned in every home, every church, every legislature. The economic interests invested in the practice are formidable. The moral imperative to end it is overwhelming. The nation must choose which master it will serve.

choices.text: Abolish slavery immediately and unconditionally — justice cannot wait
Gradual emancipation with compensation for owners — a measured path to justice
Maintain the institution — the economic consequences of abolition would be catastrophic

name: The Great Exhibition
text: Your nation has been chosen to host the first international exhibition of industry, science, and culture — a gathering of nations under a single roof of glass and iron so vast that it has been dubbed the Crystal Palace. The world's greatest inventors, engineers, artists, and industrialists will converge to display their finest achievements. The event promises to be a spectacle of unprecedented scale and a showcase of national prestige. The eyes of the world will be upon you, and the opportunity to demonstrate your civilization's preeminence is extraordinary.

choices.text: Spare no expense — make this the grandest exhibition the world has ever seen
Host a respectable exhibition within reasonable means
Focus on industrial and scientific displays — let innovation speak for itself

name: Civil War
text: The bonds that held the nation together have snapped. A coalition of provinces, citing irreconcilable differences over taxation, slavery, states' rights, or some combustible combination of all three, has declared secession and raised its own flag. The central government refuses to accept the dissolution of the union. Armies are forming on both sides of the dividing line. Brother faces brother across the barrel of a musket. The conflict that is about to unfold will be the bloodiest in the nation's history, and its outcome will determine whether the nation survives at all.

choices.text: Fight to preserve the union at all costs — the nation must not be divided

choices.text: Negotiate a peaceful separation — let them go and avoid the bloodshed
Offer a compromise — address their grievances while preserving the union

name: The Renaissance
text: A rebirth of art, learning, and human potential is transforming the nation from the ground up. The rediscovery of ancient texts has ignited a passion for the wisdom of antiquity. Wealthy patrons are commissioning works of breathtaking beauty from painters, sculptors, and architects whose names will echo through the corridors of time. The human form is being rendered with a realism and tenderness that brings viewers to tears. Cities are being redesigned with symmetry, proportion, and grace. The very concept of what it means to be human is being reexamined, redefined, and elevated.

choices.text: Become the greatest patron of the arts the world has ever known
Invest in both art and science — let beauty and knowledge flourish together
Let the Renaissance unfold naturally — genius does not require a royal invitation

name: Tsunami
text: The ocean has retreated from the shore with an unnatural haste, exposing hundreds of meters of seabed that has not seen daylight since the dawn of the world. Fish flop on the wet sand. Children chase them, laughing, unaware of what is coming. Then, on the horizon, a line of white — not a wave, but a wall of water taller than any building in the nation, moving faster than a galloping horse. The sea has returned with a fury that beggars description. It strikes the coast with the force of a cosmic hammer, surging inland for miles, carrying ships, buildings, and human beings before it like so many leaves in a flood.

choices.text: Launch a massive international relief and reconstruction effort
Rebuild with tsunami defenses — ensure this destruction is never repeated
Abandon the coastal regions and relocate the population inland

name: The Great Wall
text: Your military advisors have proposed a project of breathtaking ambition: a wall so vast, so fortified, and so monumental that it will stretch across the entire northern frontier of the nation, from sea to sea, from mountain to desert. It will require the labor of hundreds of thousands of workers over decades. It will consume resources that could build cities, fund armies, or feed populations. But when complete, it will stand as the greatest defensive structure ever conceived by human minds — a barrier so formidable that no invading army will dare to test it.

choices.text: Build the wall — let it stand as an eternal sentinel against our enemies
Build a smaller, strategic fortification network — defense without bankruptcy
Invest in the army instead — walls can be breached, but soldiers can adapt
