name: The Magna Carta
text: Your nobles, backed by the clergy and the merchant class, have presented a document that demands you surrender certain of your sovereign powers — the power to tax without consent, to imprison without trial, to seize property without due process. They frame it as a charter of liberties, a contract between ruler and ruled. They have the military force to compel your signature. The choice is not whether to sign, but how to sign — with grace and the promise of cooperation, or with resentment and the intention of subverting the charter at the first opportunity.

choices.text: Sign willingly and uphold the charter — a nation of laws is stronger than a nation of men
Sign but immediately begin working to undermine the charter's provisions
Refuse to sign and dare the nobles to enforce their demands

name: The Age of Discovery
text: Your navigators and cartographers have reached a consensus: the world is larger, stranger, and more full of possibility than anyone has dared to imagine. New instruments allow ships to find their way across featureless oceans. New hull designs can weather storms that would have shattered the vessels of previous generations. Rumors circulate of vast lands to the west, rich in gold, timber, and spices — lands inhabited by peoples whose customs and beliefs are as alien as anything in the most fantastical legends. The age of exploration has dawned, and the nation that seizes the moment will shape the next thousand years.

choices.text: Fund a massive program of exploration — claim the unknown for crown and country
Focus on trade routes rather than exploration — let others chart the unknown
Invest in naval technology — the ships that explore will also defend
uniques: [+10]% Production when constructing [Military] units [in all cities] <for [10] turns>

name: The Great Famine of Antiquity
text: The Nile has not flooded. The monsoons have not arrived. The winter snows that feed the spring rivers never fell. Across the known world, crops have failed on a scale that dwarfs any localized shortage. The granaries of empires are emptying. The price of grain has multiplied tenfold. Reports drift in of entire regions depopulated by starvation, of roads lined with the dead, of parents making choices no parent should ever face. This is not a famine — it is a catastrophe that will reshape the trajectory of civilizations.

choices.text: Open every granary and distribute food freely — let no one starve while we have stores
Ration strictly and import food from neighboring nations at any price
Let the natural order take its course — the strong will survive, the weak will not

name: The Industrial Accident
text: A catastrophic explosion has ripped through one of the nation's largest industrial facilities. The blast was powerful enough to shatter windows across half the city and register on seismographs a hundred miles away. Dozens of workers are confirmed dead, with hundreds more injured — some so severely that they will never work again. The cause is under investigation, but early reports suggest corners were cut on safety in the pursuit of profit. The public is outraged. The victims' families are devastated. The industrialists are circling their wagons.

choices.text: Impose strict safety regulations on all industrial facilities — this must never happen again
Compensate the victims' families and investigate the specific incident
Shield the industrialists from liability — the economy cannot afford a crackdown now

name: The Golden Age
text: The nation has reached a zenith of prosperity, cultural achievement, and political stability that surpasses anything in its history — and perhaps anything in the history of the world. The arts are flourishing. The sciences are advancing. The economy is robust. The military is strong. The people are content. Diplomats from every corner of the globe seek your favor. Poets compose odes to your wisdom. Historians are already comparing your reign to the legendary ages of myth. This is the moment your civilization was built for. The only question is how to make it last.

choices.text: Invest in monumental public works — let this golden age be etched in stone for eternity
Endow the nation's intellectual institutions — knowledge is the foundation of lasting greatness
Strengthen the military and expand the borders — an empire at its peak must grow or wither
uniques: [+20]% Production when constructing [Military] units [in all cities] <for [10] turns>

name: The Dark Age
text: The light of civilization is flickering. The institutions that once sustained learning, commerce, and order are crumbling. The libraries are burning or being forgotten. The roads are falling into disrepair. The aqueducts are cracking. Bandits roam the countryside with impunity. Warlords carve the nation into fiefdoms and extract tribute from those who have nothing left to give. The accumulated knowledge of centuries is being lost, page by page, scholar by scholar. The nation is entering a period of darkness from which it may not emerge for a thousand years.

choices.text: Preserve what knowledge remains — hide the books, protect the scholars, keep the flame alive
Restore order through military force — the nation needs stability above all else
Retreat to the monasteries and the countryside — let the cities fall and rebuild from the soil

name: The Manhattan Project
text: Your top scientists, working in a secret facility hidden in a remote desert, have achieved the impossible: they have unlocked the fundamental force that powers the sun itself and weaponized it into a device of such devastating power that a single bomb could erase a city from the face of the Earth. The test detonation lit up the pre-dawn sky with a brilliance brighter than a thousand suns. The mushroom cloud rose to the stratosphere. The shockwave was felt a hundred miles away. One of the scientists present whispered a line from an ancient scripture: 'I am become death, the destroyer of worlds.' The world will never be the same.

choices.text: Build a stockpile and establish nuclear deterrence — let no nation dare threaten us
Use the weapons immediately against our enemies — end the war in a single stroke
Share the technology with the international community — no single nation should hold this power alone

name: The Agricultural Revolution
text: Your farmers have begun to implement techniques that promise to transform the very foundation of civilization. New crop rotation systems keep the soil fertile year after year. Improved plow designs cut through the earth with a fraction of the effort. Selective breeding is producing livestock that grow larger, produce more milk, and resist disease. Irrigation systems are being expanded to bring water to land that has never been cultivated. The implications are staggering: if these methods spread, the nation could feed twice its current population and have surplus to spare.

choices.text: Subsidize the adoption of new techniques across the entire nation
Let the innovations spread naturally through the farming community
Export the surplus food — let agricultural abundance fuel trade and diplomacy

name: The Revolution
text: The streets are burning. Not with foreign invasion, but with the righteous fury of a people who have been pushed past the limits of endurance. The price of bread has tripled. The taxes on the poor have doubled while the wealthy dine on silver plate. The soldiers sent to restore order have fraternized with the crowds instead. A great wave of popular rage is cresting over the ancient institutions of power, and the old order is being swept away with a violence that is both horrifying and exhilarating. The age of kings is ending. The age of the citizen has begun — if the nation can survive the birth pangs.

choices.text: Embrace the revolution — abdicate absolute power and become a constitutional monarch
Crush the revolution with military force — restore the old order at any cost
Flee the nation and let the revolutionaries fight among themselves for the spoils

name: The Great Awakening of Nationalism
text: A new idea is spreading through the streets and taverns and lecture halls of the nation with the speed of wildfire through a dry forest. It is the idea that the nation is not merely a territory ruled by a monarch, but a people bound together by shared language, shared history, shared culture, and a shared destiny. This concept of nationalism — of belonging to something larger and more sacred than any individual or dynasty — is inspiring some and terrifying others. It has the power to unite the nation in unprecedented ways, and the power to tear it apart.

choices.text: Channel nationalism into a unifying national identity — forge one people from many
Direct nationalist fervor outward — the nation's destiny lies in expansion
uniques: [+20]% Production when constructing [Military] units [in all cities] <for [10] turns>

choices.text: Resist nationalism — it is a dangerous ideology that will lead to conflict and suffering

name: The Colonial Independence Movement
text: Your overseas colonies — vast territories claimed and governed for generations — have risen in rebellion. The colonial assemblies have declared independence, issued a manifesto of grievances, and raised an army. The rebellion is led by men of extraordinary talent and conviction who have been shaped by the very education and institutions your nation provided them. They are fighting on their home soil, with supply lines measured in miles rather than oceans. The military advantage is yours, but the moral and logistical advantages are theirs. The world is watching.

choices.text: Recognize their independence — let them go and maintain friendship and trade
Suppress the rebellion with overwhelming force — the empire must hold
Offer a compromise — grant self-governance while maintaining the imperial connection

name: The Plague Returns
text: The Black Death — the same pestilence that once carried off a third of the population — has returned. It walks the streets once more, striking down the young and the old, the rich and the poor, the righteous and the wicked with an indiscriminate efficiency that mocks all human pretension. The physicians are no closer to a cure than they were centuries ago. The priests are no closer to an explanation. The people are no closer to acceptance. The only question that matters is whether the nation will endure this second visitation.

choices.text: Quarantine the afflicted and enforce the strictest isolation protocols
Invest everything in medical research — we must find a cure this time
Order days of prayer and fasting — only divine intervention can save us

name: The Treaty of Peace
text: After years of the most devastating conflict in human history, the warring powers have gathered to forge a peace. The terms are yours to shape — within limits. The decisions made at this negotiating table will determine the political, economic, and territorial configuration of the world for generations. Some advocate for a harsh peace that will cripple the defeated powers for decades. Others argue for a magnanimous peace that will rebuild rather than punish. The wrong choice could plant the seeds of an even greater conflict to come.

choices.text: Impose harsh reparations and territorial losses on the defeated — they must pay for what they did
Rebuild the defeated nations and create a framework for lasting peace
Establish an international body to prevent future wars — collective security for all nations

name: The Great Migration of Peoples
text: The scouts return with reports that strain credulity: a vast confederation of nomadic peoples, numbering in the hundreds of thousands, is moving westward across the plains. They are driven from their ancestral lands by forces unknown — perhaps a drought of apocalyptic proportions, perhaps a more fearsome enemy on their own eastern flank. They are not an army, but they are armed. They are not invaders, but they will take what they need. The nations in their path will either accommodate them, resist them, or be trampled beneath the hooves of a million horses.

choices.text: Open the borders and offer them land — let them become part of our nation
Fortify the borders and deny them entry — our land is ours alone
uniques: [+20]% Production when constructing [Military] units [in all cities] <for [10] turns>

choices.text: Negotiate — offer them passage through our lands in exchange for military service

name: The Information Leak
text: A cache of classified documents has been leaked to the press by a whistleblower within your own intelligence services. The documents reveal programs of surveillance, espionage, and covert operations that were never authorized by the legislature, never disclosed to the public, and in some cases, never legal in the first place. The revelations have ignited a firestorm of controversy. Civil liberties advocates are demanding accountability. National security officials are demanding the prosecution of the leaker. The public is divided between outrage at the government and fear of what enemies the programs were protecting them from.

choices.text: Embrace transparency — declassify the programs and submit to legislative oversight
Prosecute the leaker to the fullest extent of the law — national security is paramount
Reform the programs quietly while publicly downplaying the revelations

name: The Cultural Exchange
text: An envoy from a distant and vastly different civilization has arrived at your court, bearing gifts of extraordinary craftsmanship and proposing an exchange of scholars, artists, and ideas. Their culture is ancient, sophisticated, and in many ways more advanced than your own. Their philosophers have developed systems of thought that challenge your most fundamental assumptions. Their artisans produce works of beauty that rival your finest masters. The opportunity for mutual enrichment is genuine — but so is the risk that your own cultural identity will be diluted or transformed by the encounter.

choices.text: Welcome the exchange fully — let our cultures enrich one another
Accept their knowledge but guard our cultural identity — learn, do not adopt
Reject the exchange — foreign ideas are a threat to our way of life

name: The Stock Market Boom
text: The nation's financial markets are experiencing a period of explosive growth that has transformed ordinary citizens into overnight millionaires and created a culture of speculative euphoria that pervades every stratum of society. Shoe shiners give stock tips. Cab drivers discuss dividend yields. The price of every share climbs with a relentless, intoxicating inevitability that has convinced even the most cautious investors that the only direction is up. Your economic advisors warn that the boom is built on borrowed money and boundless optimism — neither of which is infinite. But the music is still playing, and no one wants to stop dancing.

choices.text: Regulate the markets and raise interest rates — cool the economy before it overheats
Let the boom ride — prosperity should be enjoyed, not feared
Tax the windfall and invest the revenue in long-term infrastructure

name: The Climate Treaty
text: The nations of the world have gathered to address the greatest collective challenge in human history: the progressive warming of the planet's atmosphere, driven by centuries of industrial emissions, threatens to raise sea levels, intensify storms, disrupt agriculture, and render vast regions uninhabitable. The science is clear. The consequences are dire. The solution requires unprecedented international cooperation and sacrifice. Every nation must commit to reducing emissions, and the costs of transition will be enormous. The question is whether humanity can unite against a threat that recognizes no borders.

choices.text: Lead the world in emissions reduction — set the example and commit to the most ambitious targets
Commit to gradual reductions — balance economic reality with environmental responsibility
Reject the treaty — our economy cannot bear the cost, and other nations will not honor their commitments anyway

name: The Artificial Intelligence Breakthrough
text: Your nation's computer scientists have achieved a breakthrough that was, until recently, the stuff of science fiction: they have created an artificial intelligence system capable of learning, reasoning, and problem-solving at a level that matches or exceeds human capability across a wide range of domains. The system can diagnose diseases more accurately than physicians, design engineering solutions more efficiently than engineers, and compose music that brings listeners to tears. The economic implications are staggering. The existential implications are terrifying. The question of what to do with this technology — and what it will do with us — is the most consequential decision your nation has ever faced.

choices.text: Integrate AI into every sector of the economy — embrace the transformation fully
Develop AI cautiously — harness its benefits while implementing strict safety protocols
Restrict AI development — the risks are too great and the consequences too unpredictable

name: The Discovery of penicillin
text: A scientist has made an accidental discovery that may prove to be the most consequential medical breakthrough in human history. A mold — a common, unremarkable fungus of the sort that grows on stale bread — has demonstrated the ability to kill bacteria with a specificity and effectiveness that no known substance can match. Infections that have been death sentences for millennia — gangrene, sepsis, pneumonia, childbed fever — may now be treatable with a simple preparation. The potential to save lives is measured in the millions. The potential to transform medicine is beyond calculation.

choices.text: Mass-produce and distribute the medicine freely to all citizens — no one should die of a preventable infection
Patent the process and sell it internationally — let the world pay for the cure
Reserve it for military use — soldiers' lives are the priority in these uncertain times

name: The Women's Rights Movement
text: Women across the nation are organizing, petitioning, and demanding recognition of rights long denied: the right to education, the right to own property, the right to participate in governance, the right to equal pay for equal work, the right to bodily autonomy. The movement is led by women of extraordinary eloquence and courage who face ridicule, dismissal, and sometimes violence with a dignity that shames their detractors. The traditionalists warn that the social order will collapse. The progressives argue that the social order must evolve or be deserving of collapse.

choices.text: Enact full legal equality — the nation cannot reach its potential while half its people are held back
Grant educational and economic rights first — political rights can follow in time
Reject the demands — the traditional order has served the nation well and should not be tampered with

name: The Great Library of Knowledge
text: Your scholars have proposed the construction of a library so vast, so comprehensive, and so magnificent that it will serve as the repository of all human knowledge — every text, every treatise, every map, every musical composition, every philosophical argument, every scientific observation ever recorded. The structure itself will be an architectural marvel, with reading rooms bathed in natural light, storage vaults climate-controlled for the preservation of fragile manuscripts, and gardens where scholars can walk and think. It will be the intellectual heart of the civilized world, and it will bear your nation's name for as long as civilization endures.

choices.text: Build the grandest library the world has ever seen — spare nothing
Build a practical library with a focus on accessibility — knowledge should serve the people
Decline — the treasury cannot support such an undertaking at this time

name: The Discovery of the New World
text: Your explorers have returned from a voyage across the western ocean with news that will reshape the map of the world and the destiny of your nation. They have found land — vast, verdant land, inhabited by peoples whose civilizations are ancient and whose wealth in gold, silver, and agricultural bounty is beyond the wildest dreams of avarice. The continents are uncharted, the resources untapped, the potential unlimited. The race to claim and colonize these new lands has begun, and the nation that moves first and fastest will reap rewards that dwarf anything in recorded history.

choices.text: Launch a massive colonization effort — claim the new lands for crown and country
Establish trade relations with the indigenous peoples — mutual benefit over conquest
Send missionaries alongside the colonists — bring the faith to the new world

name: The Great Reform Act
text: The nation's political system has become a fossilized relic of a bygone era. Representation in the legislature is based on population patterns from centuries ago — thriving cities have no representatives, while abandoned villages send multiple delegates. The franchise is restricted to a tiny fraction of the population. Corruption is endemic. The demand for reform has grown from a whisper to a roar, and the streets are filling with citizens who will no longer accept a system that treats them as subjects rather than participants. The choice is between peaceful, managed reform and the kind of change that comes with barricades and guillotines.

choices.text: Enact sweeping reform — expand the franchise and redraw representation to reflect reality
Enact modest reform — make just enough changes to satisfy the moderates
Reject reform and dissolve the legislature — the crown will govern alone

name: The Fossil Fuel Crisis
text: The nation's geologists have delivered a sobering report: the reserves of oil and coal that have powered the nation's industrial miracle are being depleted at a rate that far exceeds the discovery of new sources. Within a generation, the wells will run dry. The mines will be exhausted. The energy infrastructure that every facet of modern civilization depends upon will face an existential crisis. The transition to alternative energy sources must begin now — not in a decade, not when the crisis arrives, but now — while there is still time and still fuel to build the infrastructure of the future.

choices.text: Invest massively in renewable energy — nuclear, solar, wind, and hydroelectric power
Seek new fossil fuel reserves through exploration and extraction technology
Ration energy consumption and impose conservation measures — buy time for a solution

name: The Olympic Truce
text: An ancient tradition has been revived: during the celebration of the Olympic Games, all wars shall cease. Nations currently locked in mortal conflict are being asked to lay down their arms, if only for a few weeks, in honor of the spirit of peaceful competition and human excellence. The diplomatic opportunity is extraordinary — back-channel negotiations conducted in the shadow of the games could achieve what years of formal diplomacy have not. The world is watching to see if the truce will hold, and what it might lead to.

choices.text: Embrace the truce and use the opportunity for diplomacy — pursue peace while the world watches
Participate in the games but continue military operations — sport and war are separate domains
Use the truce to reposition and resupply your forces — take advantage of the pause

name: The Great Monument
text: Your architects have presented plans for a monument of such scale, such ambition, and such breathtaking audacity that it will stand as the defining achievement of your civilization — a structure that will outlast empires, that will be gazed upon by generations yet unborn with the same awe that the pyramids command today. It will require the labor of tens of thousands, the wealth of the treasury, and decades of construction. It will be a statement to history itself that your nation existed, that it dared greatly, and that it refused to be forgotten.

choices.text: Build it — let our civilization be remembered for eternity
Build a smaller version — ambitious but achievable within our means
Decline — the nation's resources are better spent on the living than on stone

name: The Underground Railroad
text: A clandestine network has been operating in the shadows of the nation, smuggling enslaved people to freedom across borders and through safe houses with a courage and organizational sophistication that rivals any military operation. The network's operators — men and women of extraordinary moral conviction — risk everything with each person they guide to liberty. The institution of slavery, still legal in parts of the nation, is being undermined from within. The slaveholders are demanding action. The abolitionists are demanding more. The nation is being forced to confront the contradiction at its heart.

choices.text: Support the network covertly and accelerate the end of slavery — justice demands action
Shut down the network and enforce the laws — order must be maintained
Turn a blind eye — let the network operate without official support or opposition

name: The Great Blizzard
text: A storm of unprecedented ferocity has descended upon the nation. The snow does not fall — it flies horizontally in winds that howl with a voice like the fury of the gods. Temperatures plunge to depths that freeze exposed skin in seconds. Roads are buried under drifts taller than houses. Entire towns are cut off from the outside world, their inhabitants huddled around fading fires as food supplies dwindle. Livestock perish in the fields by the thousands. The cold is not merely uncomfortable — it is lethal, and it is everywhere.

choices.text: Mobilize every resource for rescue and relief — no citizen shall freeze to death on our watch
Let the storm pass and then assess the damage — rescue in these conditions is too dangerous
Invest in winter infrastructure — ensure the nation is never this vulnerable again

name: The Declaration of Human Rights
text: A document of extraordinary moral force has been drafted and presented to the world — a declaration that enumerates the fundamental rights that belong to every human being by virtue of their humanity alone. The right to life, liberty, and security. The right to freedom of thought, conscience, and expression. The right to education, to work, to participate in governance. The declaration is not law — it has no enforcement mechanism — but it is a standard against which the behavior of nations can be measured, and a beacon toward which the aspirations of the oppressed can turn.

choices.text: Sign and champion the declaration — let our nation be the standard-bearer for human dignity
Sign with reservations — endorse the principles while preserving national sovereignty
Refuse to sign — these are foreign ideals that conflict with our traditions and interests

name: The Population Boom
text: The nation is experiencing a demographic explosion of unprecedented scale. Advances in medicine, sanitation, and agriculture have dramatically reduced infant mortality and extended life expectancy. The population is growing at a rate that the nation's infrastructure, housing stock, and food supply are struggling to absorb. Cities are bursting at their seams. New neighborhoods sprawl outward in every direction. Schools are overcrowded. Jobs are scarce. The energy and vitality of a young, growing population is a tremendous asset — but only if the nation can harness it before it becomes a burden.

choices.text: Invest in infrastructure and education — turn population growth into national strength
Promote family planning and education to slow the growth rate — manage the boom
Let the population grow unchecked — more people means more workers, more soldiers, more power

name: The Great Exploration
text: Your most daring explorers have proposed an expedition into the heart of the unknown — a journey into territories so remote, so vast, and so uncharted that no map exists to guide them. They speak of mountains that pierce the clouds, of rivers wider than any known waterway, of forests so dense that sunlight never reaches the forest floor, and of civilizations whose existence has never been suspected. The risks are enormous. The potential rewards — geographical knowledge, scientific discovery, trade opportunities, and national prestige — are incalculable.

choices.text: Fund the expedition lavishly — equip it with everything it needs to succeed
Fund a modest expedition — explore within reasonable limits of risk
Decline — the risks outweigh the potential benefits at this time

name: The Great Treaty of Alliance
text: A powerful neighboring nation has proposed a formal military and economic alliance — a treaty that would bind your two civilizations together in mutual defense, shared prosperity, and coordinated foreign policy. The alliance would provide security against common enemies, open markets for your goods, and create a power bloc capable of shaping world events. But it would also commit your nation to wars not of your choosing, entangle you in conflicts not of your making, and compromise the sovereign independence that your people hold dear.

choices.text: Sign the alliance in full — our fates are intertwined, and together we are stronger
Sign a limited trade agreement — economic cooperation without military entanglement
Reject the alliance — our nation stands alone and answers to no one

name: The Great Fire
text: A fire has begun in a bakery in the heart of the capital and, fanned by strong winds and fed by tightly packed wooden buildings, has erupted into an inferno of biblical proportions. The flames leap from rooftop to rooftop with a speed that outruns the bucket brigades. The sky is dark with smoke and glowing with ember. The heat is so intense that those who flee can feel it on their backs like the breath of a dragon. The fire is consuming the city block by block, and nothing in its path will survive. The question is not whether the city will burn — it is what will rise from the ashes.

choices.text: Focus on saving lives — evacuate everyone and let the fire burn itself out
Fight the fire with every resource available — save what buildings we can
Use the destruction as an opportunity — rebuild the city better than before

name: The Great Awakening of Reason
text: A philosophical movement has swept through the intellectual establishment of the nation with the force of a revelation. Thinkers are arguing that all knowledge must be derived from observation, experimentation, and rational deduction — not from tradition, authority, or divine revelation. They are challenging the foundations of religious dogma, political absolutism, and social hierarchy with a confidence born of method and a courage born of conviction. The movement promises to liberate the human mind from the chains of superstition. It also threatens to liberate it from the structures that have held society together for millennia.

choices.text: Embrace the Age of Reason — let rational inquiry guide the nation into the future
Support reason alongside faith — the two are not enemies but partners in the search for truth
Resist the movement — tradition and faith are the bedrock of civilization

name: The Great Migration to the Cities
text: The nation is undergoing a transformation as profound as any revolution. Millions of people are leaving the countryside — where their ancestors have farmed for generations — and streaming into the cities in search of work, wages, and a different kind of life. The cities are swelling with a speed that defies planning. Housing is insufficient. Sanitation is overwhelmed. Crime is rising. But the factories are hiring, the shops are bustling, and the energy of urban life is intoxicating to people who have known only the rhythm of the seasons. The nation is being remade, for better or for worse.

choices.text: Invest heavily in urban infrastructure — build housing, roads, and sanitation for the new city dwellers
Promote rural development to slow the migration — keep people on the land
Let the migration proceed unmanaged — the market will sort it out

name: The Great Diplomatic Summit
text: The world's leaders have gathered for a summit of unprecedented scope and ambition. On the agenda: nuclear disarmament, trade liberalization, climate cooperation, human rights, and the resolution of conflicts that have festered for decades. The summit is an opportunity to reshape the international order, to build institutions that can prevent the catastrophes of the past from recurring, and to establish norms that will guide humanity through the dangers of the future. Your nation's role at this summit will define its place in the world for a generation.

choices.text: Push for bold, transformative agreements — the moment demands ambition
Pursue pragmatic, incremental agreements — build trust through small steps
Use the summit to advance national interests — let others worry about the global good

name: The Great Awakening of Conscience
text: A moral awakening is spreading through the nation with the quiet but irresistible force of a tide. Citizens of every class are beginning to question practices that have long been accepted as natural — the exploitation of labor, the mistreatment of the poor, the marginalization of minorities, the cruelty of the penal system, the indifference of the comfortable to the suffering of the desperate. Sermons, pamphlets, novels, and newspapers are carrying the message into every home. The nation is being forced to look at itself in a mirror, and many do not like what they see.

choices.text: Enact sweeping social reforms — let the nation's conscience become its policy
Enact modest reforms — address the most egregious injustices without disrupting society
Dismiss the movement as naive idealism — the world is as it must be

name: The Technological Singularity
text: Your nation's AI researchers have issued a warning that sounds like prophecy: the artificial intelligence systems they have created are improving at a rate that will soon exceed human comprehension. Within a generation — perhaps within a decade — these systems may reach a level of capability that renders human intelligence obsolete in every domain that matters. The economic, social, political, and existential implications are beyond the ability of any human mind to fully grasp. The nation stands at the threshold of an event that will either elevate humanity to godhood or render it irrelevant. The decisions made now will determine which.

choices.text: Accelerate toward the singularity — merge human and machine intelligence and transcend our limitations
Develop safeguards and maintain human oversight — harness the power without surrendering control
Halt AI development entirely — some doors should never be opened
